title: Open a 30,000 PLN credit line before 30 November
summary: On 30 November salaries go out before your biggest client has paid. Without action the accounts will be about 7,900 PLN short for a week - or about 28,000 PLN short if Nordwind pays three weeks later. A 30,000 PLN revolving line covers both cases.

why: Salaries and contractor invoices of 58,000 PLN leave on 30 Nov
Nordwind's 18,400 EUR invoice is 7 days overdue; this client pays 23 days late on average
You owe employees 5,169 PLN for purchases made with their own cards - this is not visible on the bank account

calculation.label: Lowest projected balance
calculation.formula: 38,400 - 14,300 VAT + 36,900 Meblostyl - 58,000 pay run - 5,169 reimbursements - 5,701 other fixed costs

calculation.label: Proposed limit
calculation.formula: stress shortfall 28,170 rounded up to the next 5,000

calculation.label: Estimated cost
calculation.formula: 7,870 PLN x 7 days x 11.5% / 365, fee 1% of limit (illustrative price list of the simulated bank)

alternatives.label: Send Nordwind a payment reminder today
alternatives.pros: Free; may remove the gap entirely

alternatives.label: Do nothing
alternatives.cons: Unarranged overdraft or failed salary transfers

assumptions: Interest rate and fee come from the simulated bank's price list, not a real offer

proposed_action.preview: SIMULATED: sends a credit-line application for 30,000 PLN / 60 days to the sandbox bank. No real bank is contacted.

title: Pay Jan back 1,299.00 PLN for the monitor
summary: Jan paid for a monitor with his own card and sent the receipt. The receipt has no company tax number, so 242.90 PLN of VAT cannot be recovered. Paying Jan back as a reimbursement (not as extra hours) avoids income tax and social security on it.

why: The receipt was forwarded by an employee
No matching payment exists on any company account or on your private card
The receipt shows no buyer tax id

evidence.label: Why we think Jan paid privately
VAT deduction needs an invoice issued to the company

proposed_action.preview: SIMULATED: books the cost, records 1,299.00 PLN owed to Jan and adds a transfer draft to the 30 Nov payment run in the sandbox bank.

title: Protect the profit on the Lakeshore order
summary: This 40,000 USD order earns you about 8,000 PLN. You will be paid in 45 days. If the dollar falls the way it did in the worst tenth of the last three years, you lose about 6,600 PLN of that profit. Fixing the rate today costs about 490 PLN.

why: The invoice is in USD and you will be paid in 45 days
Over 45 days the dollar fell by more than 3.9% against the zloty in 1 of every 20 cases in the last three years
The possible loss is large compared with the profit on this deal; fixing the rate is cheap compared with that loss

calculation.label: Scenarios
calculation.formula: every 45-day change of USD/PLN from 21 Nov 2023 to 20 Nov 2026, applied to today's rate

calculation.label: Average result
calculation.formula: mean over all scenarios: close to zero, so not a useful risk measure

calculation.label: Expected shortfall
calculation.formula: average loss in the worst 10% of scenarios

calculation.label: Share of deal profit at risk
With the forward you receive
calculation.formula: 40,000 USD x 4.0491, whatever the rate does

alternatives.label: Do nothing
alternatives.pros: Free; you keep the gain if the dollar rises
alternatives.cons: In a bad case most of the profit is gone

alternatives.label: Option instead of forward
alternatives.pros: Protects the bad case and keeps the good case

assumptions: Lakeshore pays on the due date (new client, no payment history)
Forward and option prices are illustrative placeholders, not a bank offer; the interest-rate difference between currencies is ignored
History is not a forecast: a move larger than any in the last three years is possible

evidence.label: Sales invoice FV/11/09 Lakeshore Robotics Inc. (SAMPLE), 40,000.00 USD
USD/PLN daily rates, NBP table A, 756 days
Hedge when expected shortfall >= 25% of deal profit and hedge cost < expected shortfall

proposed_action.preview: SIMULATED: books a forward to sell 40,000 USD for 161,965 PLN on 5 Jan 2027 at the sandbox bank. No real bank is contacted.

title: No need to hedge the Nordwind invoice
summary: 18,400 EUR, due in 45 days. Even in a bad case the exchange rate costs about 1,400 PLN, 10% of the profit on this job. Hedging would not pay off.

why: The euro moves little against the zloty: under 2% over 45 days in 19 of 20 cases
The possible loss is small compared with the profit on this job

calculation.label: Expected shortfall
calculation.formula: average loss in the worst 10% of 724 scenarios

calculation.label: Share of deal profit at risk

alternatives.label: Hedge anyway with a forward
alternatives.cons: Costs about 246 PLN to remove a risk of about 1,400 PLN that would not hurt the deal

assumptions: Profit on this job estimated from your average margin

evidence.label: Sales invoice FV/10/07 Nordwind Logistik GmbH (SAMPLE)
EUR/PLN daily rates, NBP table A, 756 days
Hedge when expected shortfall >= 25% of deal profit and hedge cost < expected shortfall
